Bootstrap Intervals for the Coefficients of a Fit

Source: R/bootstrap_interval.R
bootstrap_interval.Rd

Three intervals are read from the replicates that add_bootstrap() stores in a fit: the percentile interval, the basic interval and the BCa interval. Each is an object built by percentile_interval(), basic_interval() or bca_interval(), and the object is passed as the argument interval of confint.StatmodFit().

bootstrap_interval is the abstract parent of the three classes. It cannot be instantiated, and serves to test membership with S7::S7_inherits().

Usage

bootstrap_interval(
  name = character(0),
  label = character(0),
  n = NULL,
  resample = NULL,
  refit = NULL
)

PercentileInterval(
  name = character(0),
  label = character(0),
  n = NULL,
  resample = NULL,
  refit = NULL
)

BasicInterval(
  name = character(0),
  label = character(0),
  n = NULL,
  resample = NULL,
  refit = NULL
)

BcaInterval(
  name = character(0),
  label = character(0),
  n = NULL,
  resample = NULL,
  refit = NULL
)

percentile_interval(n = NULL, resample = NULL, refit = NULL)

basic_interval(n = NULL, resample = NULL, refit = NULL)

bca_interval(n = NULL, resample = NULL, refit = NULL)

Arguments

name

A single string, the short name of the interval.

label

A single string, the name under which an object prints.

n

A single whole number, the total number of replicates, or NULL.

resample

A resample_method object, or NULL.

refit

"coefficients", "full" or NULL.

Value

percentile_interval(), basic_interval() and bca_interval() return an object that inherits from bootstrap_interval, with the properties name, label, n, resample and refit. bootstrap_interval returns nothing: its constructor signals an error.

Details

Write \(\hat\theta\) for an estimate, \(\theta^*_{(\alpha)}\) for the \(\alpha\) quantile of its bootstrap replicates and \(\alpha = 1 -\) level. The percentile interval is $$[\theta^*_{(\alpha/2)},\; \theta^*_{(1 - \alpha/2)}],$$ and the basic interval is $$[2\hat\theta - \theta^*_{(1 - \alpha/2)},\; 2\hat\theta - \theta^*_{(\alpha/2)}],$$ the reflection of the percentile interval about the estimate (Davison and Hinkley 1997, chapter 5). The quantiles are those of stats::quantile() with its default type.

The BCa interval (bias-corrected and accelerated) takes the quantiles of the replicates at adjusted levels, $$\Phi\!\left(z_0 + \frac{z_0 + z_{\alpha'}}{1 - a\,(z_0 + z_{\alpha'})} \right), \quad \alpha' \in \{\alpha/2,\; 1 - \alpha/2\},$$ where \(\Phi\) is the standard normal distribution function and \(z_{\alpha'}\) its quantile. The bias correction \(z_0 = \Phi^{-1}(\hat p)\) uses the proportion \(\hat p\) of replicates below the estimate, with the replicates equal to it counted by halves. The acceleration is $$a = \frac{\sum_i (\bar\theta_{(\cdot)} - \hat\theta_{(-i)})^3} {6\,[\sum_i (\bar\theta_{(\cdot)} - \hat\theta_{(-i)})^2]^{3/2}},$$ with \(\hat\theta_{(-i)}\) the estimate of the fit refitted without observation \(i\) (the weight of the observation set to zero) and \(\bar\theta_{(\cdot)}\) the mean of these estimates (Efron 1987). With cluster_resample() the unit deleted is a cluster. The refits are made once and stored in the entry, one per observation or cluster, with the settings of the entry (refit), so that the first call of confint.StatmodFit() costs as many refits as there are units, and later calls read them. The interval is available for case_resample(), cluster_resample() and bayesian_resample(). parametric_resample() is rejected, because the acceleration needs the influence of the observations of the data, and so is cluster_resample() beside a modelterms7::random() term. A coordinate whose estimate lies outside the range of its replicates, or whose adjusted level is undefined, has NA limits.

The quantity is the one that confint.StatmodFit() reports. With readable = TRUE the readable quantities are computed on every replicate and the quantiles are taken afterwards, so the percentile interval of a transformed quantity is the transformed percentile interval. A coordinate that is missing in some replicate (the individual random effects under cluster_resample()) or in the fit (an aliased coefficient) has NA limits.

The replicates are those of the stored entry that the arguments select, in the way bootstrap_vcov() selects it: a NULL argument takes the value of the single entry that matches the others, and the defaults when none matches. An entry with fewer than n replicates is extended, and one with more is read up to its first n. The default when nothing is stored is n = 1000, because a tail of a 95 per cent interval holds only one replicate in forty. A warning is signaled when a tail holds fewer than ten replicates, that is, when \(n \alpha / 2 < 10\).

References

Davison, A. C. and Hinkley, D. V. (1997). Bootstrap Methods and Their Application. Cambridge University Press.

Efron, B. (1987). Better bootstrap confidence intervals. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 82(397), 171–185.

See also

confint.StatmodFit(), add_bootstrap(), bootstrap_vcov().

Examples

set.seed(1)
dd <- data.frame(x = runif(40))
dd$y <- 1 + 2 * dd$x + rnorm(40, sd = 0.4)
fit <- statmod(y ~ x, distributions7::gaussian1_distrib(), dd)
fit <- add_bootstrap(fit, n = 60, resample = case_resample())
confint(fit, interval = percentile_interval(n = 60))
#> Warning: The 60 replicates leave 1.5 in each tail of a 95 per cent interval.
#>   The quantiles of a tail are unstable below 10 replicates: use n of at least 400.
#>                   parameter   term coefficient  estimate         se      lower
#> mu:(Intercept)           mu linpar (Intercept)  1.120104 0.09288556  0.9708948
#> mu:x                     mu linpar           x  1.818008 0.15386898  1.5431546
#> sigma:(Intercept)     sigma linpar (Intercept) -1.097264 0.12477276 -1.4334584
#>                        upper
#> mu:(Intercept)     1.3282745
#> mu:x               2.0919233
#> sigma:(Intercept) -0.9032555
confint(fit, interval = basic_interval(n = 60))
#> Warning: The 60 replicates leave 1.5 in each tail of a 95 per cent interval.
#>   The quantiles of a tail are unstable below 10 replicates: use n of at least 400.
#>                   parameter   term coefficient  estimate         se     lower
#> mu:(Intercept)           mu linpar (Intercept)  1.120104 0.09288556  0.911934
#> mu:x                     mu linpar           x  1.818008 0.15386898  1.544093
#> sigma:(Intercept)     sigma linpar (Intercept) -1.097264 0.12477276 -1.291272
#>                        upper
#> mu:(Intercept)     1.2693137
#> mu:x               2.0928620
#> sigma:(Intercept) -0.7610695
confint(fit, interval = bca_interval(n = 60))
#> Warning: The 60 replicates leave 1.5 in each tail of a 95 per cent interval.
#>   The quantiles of a tail are unstable below 10 replicates: use n of at least 400.
#> bootstrap: computed 40 refits without one observation (case, refit coefficients).
#> Warning: The BCa levels of some coordinate fall in the first or last replicate, so an extreme order statistic is a limit.
#>   Use more replicates.
#>                   parameter   term coefficient  estimate         se      lower
#> mu:(Intercept)           mu linpar (Intercept)  1.120104 0.09288556  0.9807196
#> mu:x                     mu linpar           x  1.818008 0.15386898  1.5329340
#> sigma:(Intercept)     sigma linpar (Intercept) -1.097264 0.12477276 -1.2517273
#>                        upper
#> mu:(Intercept)     1.3363865
#> mu:x               2.0761335
#> sigma:(Intercept) -0.8839039
